WhatsApp is developing a new feature that lets users connect third-party AI agents to the app, chat with them, and instruct them to perform tasks on their behalf. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing support for third-party agents

When platforms like OpenClaw first appeared, one of the main ways users controlled them remotely was by connecting agents to instant messaging apps.

However, many users later discovered that setting up bots and third-party AI agents on WhatsApp could result in their WhatsApp accounts being banned.

At the same time, Telegram seized on this trend and became one of the main platforms where users communicated with agents or issued them instructions — agents that could run on the user's local computer or be deployed in the cloud.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is introducing native support for third-party AI agents, allowing users to connect them to a specified chat window directly within the app.

After a user configures a new bot on WhatsApp, the app generates an API key that users can use to connect their agent to the chat window. WABetaInfo explains: "The specific steps depend on the platform, but most services include a field where users paste" that API key, enabling direct conversation with the third-party agent via WhatsApp.

Below is the report from WABetaInfo:

The site notes that only some Android users currently have access to this new feature, but it is expected to roll out more widely in the near term. WABetaInfo says WhatsApp's implementation supports up to five agents per account and allows users to customise the name and profile picture of each agent. However, chats with third-party agents currently do not offer end-to-end encryption.
